ROAD TO 250: The Road to Independence

On June 11, 1776, the Continental Congress recessed for three weeks and tasked a small group—Thomas Jefferson, John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, Roger Sherman, and Robert R. Livingston, known as the Committee of Five—with drafting what would become the Declaration of Independence. Jefferson wrote the first draft, with edits and input from Adams and Franklin.

Even at our founding, big ideas took collaboration.

ROAD TO 250: America’s Road to Independence

On June 11, 1776, the Continental Congress pressed pause—but the work continued. During the recess, the Committee of Five—Thomas Jefferson, John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, Roger Sherman, and Robert R. Livingston—was tasked with drafting what would become the Declaration of Independence.

A reminder that history is often made in the moments between the headlines.
